issues.description: Field StockIngredient.price is declared as double in the template implementation but is specified as int in the problem statement UML and implemented as int in the solution. The problem statement's class diagram and constructor signature indicate StockIngredient(String, int, int) and '-price: int', while template/src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java declares 'private final double price;' and a constructor taking a double. This mismatch will cause confusion and potential compilation/type issues because other APIs in the exercise (e.g., SealSaloon.calculateTotalPrice which returns int and acceptSupplyDelivery which takes an int price) expect integer prices.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template StockIngredient to use int for the price field and constructor parameter to match the problem statement and solution. Specifically: (1) declare 'private final int price;', (2) change the constructor signature to StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity), and (3) change getPrice() to return int. Ensure any code that constructs StockIngredient in the template uses int literals or casts so compilation and semantics align with the rest of the exercise.

issues.description: The exercise title in the problem statement ('H02E02 - Panic at Seal Saloon') differs from the project name set in the provided repositories. The template settings.gradle sets rootProject.name = 'H04E01---Panic-at-Burger-House' and the solution settings.gradle sets rootProject.name = 'H04E01---Panic-at-Burger-House-Solution'. This inconsistent naming between the problem statement and repository metadata can confuse students about which exercise they are working on and may lead to mismatched packaging or deliverable naming.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the exercise/project name consistent across artifacts. Either update the problem statement header to match the repositories' project name or update the template and solution settings.gradle rootProject.name to match the problem statement (e.g., 'H02E02---Panic-at-Seal-Saloon'). Ensure both template and solution use the same rootProject.name string so students are not confused.
